chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who has his wife with him on a journey and cannot find water; can he sleep with his wife? He (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not like him to do so, except if he fears upon himself.'

I said: 'Does he seek pleasure thereby, or is he craving for women?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The craving is [considered] fearing upon himself.' I said: 'He seeks pleasure thereby?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is permissible.'

I said: 'For it is reported from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that Abu Dharr (may Allah have mercy on him) asked him about this, so he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Go to your wife, you will be rewarded.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Do I go to them and get rewarded?' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Just as when you go to the forbidden, you are burdened [with sin], so similarly, when you go to the permissible, you will be rewarded.'
So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you not see that he, when he fears upon himself, so he goes to the permissible, would be rewarded?'
ai.seo_question: Can a man sleep with his wife during travel if he cannot find water for ablution?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the principle of *al-shabiq* (sexual desire) as a valid excuse for neglecting ablution during travel, reflecting the Shia emphasis on balancing spiritual rigor with natural human instincts. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the permissibility of marital intimacy in this state, countering ascetic tendencies by linking the reward for fulfilling natural desires to the burden of avoiding prohibitions, as cited from the Prophet’s dialogue with Abu Dharr. This underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that *halal* acts, when performed with proper intention, carry spiritual merit comparable to *haram* acts in terms of accountability.
